items.hook: Rage is a 1987 novel by Wilbur Smith set in the Union of South Africa, immediately following World War II.
items.body: It starts in 1952 and goes until the late 1960s, touching on the country's declaration of a republic and the subsequent Sharpeville Massacre. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Sabbatical: A Romance is a novel by the American writer John Barth, published in 1982.
items.body: The story is centered on a yacht race through the Chesapeake Bay. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Yasmin Cordery Khan is a British historian, novelist and broadcaster whose work focuses on the British Empire, Colonial India and the decolonisation of South Asia.
items.body: She is a Fellow of Kellogg College, Oxford and Professor of Modern History based in the Oxford University Department for Continuing Education. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Far Tortuga is a novel by American author Peter Matthiessen, first published in 1975 by Random House and republished in 1976 by Bantam.
items.body: Known for its unique typography and poetic prose, the novel follows the story of a group of Caribbean turtle fishermen as they sail the waters of the Cayman Islands aboard the schooner Lillias Eden. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Don't Make Waves is a 1967 American sex comedy starring Tony Curtis, Claudia Cardinale, Dave Draper and Sharon Tate.
items.body: Distributed by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, the film was directed by Alexander Mackendrick and is based on the 1959 novel Muscle Beach by Ira Wallach, who also co-wrote the screenplay. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.
